Figure 1:From logged futures to candidate-matched supervision.(1) WAM pretraining uses the ground-truth (GT) trajectory and its
logged future video.
(2) Trajectory GRPO explores candidate trajectories using driving
rewards, without matched video supervision.
(3) World Engine renders reconstructed scenes along selected candidate paths,
providing matched supervision independent of the model’s predictions.

Figure 2:Simulation-grounded video–trajectory alignment.(a) Training overview.
(b) Trajectory learning combines GRPO with a behavior-cloning (BC) regularizer.
(c) Video supervision selects high-reward, higher-error futures.
(d) World Engine renders matched futures along executed paths.

Figure 3:Planning results and video-supervision comparisons.(a) NAVSIM v1. (b) NAVSIM v2 and HUGSIM.
(c) Video-supervision configurations and rendering budget on NAVSIM v1.

Figure 4:Qualitative planning comparison.Left: planned trajectories ofSimVTA(A, blue) and Epona (B, orange).
Right: World Engine renderings along the corresponding paths at 1–4 s.
Red boxes highlight Epona’s collision and road-departure regions.

Figure 5:Matched futures for alternative actions.Left: shared observation history and executed paths for going straight (A),
changing lanes to the left (B), and changing lanes to the right (C).
Right: corresponding future frames rendered by the simulator.
Colors match the paths and image rows.

Figure 6:Video–trajectory alignment before and after post-training.Left: observation history and trajectory in BEV.
Right: World Engine renderings and predictions fromSimVTAand Epona.
